provenance: Agent-curated summaries of linked original sources; not Papiers search results, not human annotations, and not Toronto-calibrated parameters.

papers.title: Meta-analysis of public transport demand
papers.finding: Fare elasticities vary with model specification; the common -0.3 rule of thumb is conditional on service treatment.
papers.mvp_use: Do not use one universal response coefficient.
papers.transfer_limit: Meta-analysis, not a Toronto fare estimate.

papers.title: Bus elasticities and diversion factors
papers.authors: UK Department for Transport; RAND Europe and SYSTRA
papers.finding: Government synthesis reviews bus fare/time elasticities and diversion to other modes or no travel.
papers.mvp_use: Represent walk, bike, car, alternate destination and no-trip branches.
papers.transfer_limit: UK evidence; no TTC diversion shares supplied here.

papers.title: Short run fare elasticities for Bogota's BRT system: ridership responses to fare increases
papers.authors: Luis A. Guzman; Santiago Gomez; Carlos Alberto Moncada
papers.finding: Station-panel estimate is about -0.565 one week after a rise and -0.408 after a month; low-income and off-peak users were more sensitive.
papers.mvp_use: Illustrative short-run sensitivity candidate and subgroup design.
papers.transfer_limit: Bogota BRT in 2001-2012, not Toronto TTC in 2026; not a calibrated local coefficient.

papers.title: Public transport fare elasticities from smartcard data: Evidence from a natural experiment
papers.finding: Stockholm smartcard study estimates differentiated fare response by travel pair, mode and socioeconomic group.
papers.mvp_use: Differentiate persona response by constraints and distance.
papers.transfer_limit: Zone-to-flat fare reform, not a uniform increase; coefficients not transferable to TTC.

papers.title: Impact of Transit Fare Increase on Ridership and Revenue: Metropolitan Transportation Authority, New York City
papers.finding: Fare-product switching matters when different fare media change by different amounts.
papers.mvp_use: Compute paid fare by product before sample revenue.
papers.transfer_limit: NYC 2003 fare menu, not TTC cap and Fair Pass rules.

papers.title: Estimating the Price Elasticity of Demand for Subways: Evidence from Mexico
papers.finding: Fare changes across three Mexican subway systems imply elasticities of about -0.23 to -0.32.
papers.mvp_use: Alternative sensitivity anchor, not a direct TTC input.
papers.transfer_limit: Subway systems and two large 30%+ hikes or a fare holiday.

papers.title: How Low-income Transit Riders in Boston Respond to Discounted Fares: A Randomized Controlled Evaluation
papers.authors: Jeffrey Rosenblum; Jinhua Zhao; Mariana Arcaya; Justin Steil; P. Christopher Zegras
papers.finding: In a Boston randomized study, a 50% discount increased trips by about 30% and health/social-service trips increased.
papers.mvp_use: Purpose-specific affordability constraints and protected-fare subgroup.
papers.transfer_limit: Discount direction and low-income Boston sample; no established Toronto shopping response.

papers.title: Eliminating Fares to Expand Opportunities: Experimental Evidence on the Impacts of Free Public Transportation on Economic and Social Disparities
papers.authors: Rebecca Brough; Matthew Freedman; David C. Phillips
papers.finding: Temporary free fares for low-income individuals had no statistically significant effect on paid hours or earnings; financial/health evidence was suggestive.
papers.transfer_limit: Free fare, another population and system; does not estimate Toronto fare-hike effect.

papers.title: The Characteristics of Shopping Trips by Bus Transit
papers.finding: California descriptive study of shopping by bus highlights stop distance, transfers, travel time and walking environment.
papers.mvp_use: Trip purpose and destination/accessibility affect shop visits.
papers.transfer_limit: Descriptive study, not a fare-to-sales causal estimate.

papers.title: Impacts of CBD Fare-Free Transit on Retail Sales
papers.authors: Terry J. Atherton; Ellyn S. Eder
papers.finding: Albany sales-tax panel of 115 retailers suggests positive effects of downtown fare-free transit for some shop types/seasons and shops near routes.
papers.mvp_use: Plausible but uncertain local access-to-retail pathway.
papers.transfer_limit: Old fare removal and downtown setting; not a closure or reverse-effect estimate.

papers.title: The Free-Fare Transit Experiments
papers.finding: Off-peak free-fare evaluations raised ridership but did not noticeably change commercial and employment activity.
papers.mvp_use: Include zero retail/employment effect as a sensitivity case.
papers.transfer_limit: Old fare-removal settings, not a Toronto fare increase.

papers.title: Can transit investments in low-income neighbourhoods increase transit use? Exploring the nexus of income, car-ownership, and transit accessibility in Toronto
papers.finding: In the GTHA, transit accessibility and transit use relate differently across income and car-ownership groups.
papers.mvp_use: Toronto-context persona heterogeneity without inventing household joint records.
papers.transfer_limit: Accessibility association, not causal fare elasticity.

papers.title: Fare-Capping Impact Analysis Using Mobile Ticket Data
papers.finding: A mobile-ticket fare-product choice model accounts for switching in fare-capping/ridership/revenue analysis.
papers.mvp_use: Preserve cap and fare product in each rider's payment state.
papers.transfer_limit: Method from different agencies; no direct TTC forecast.

papers.title: Subways near the subway: Rail transit and neighborhood catering businesses in Beijing
papers.authors: Siqi Zheng; Xiaoke Hu; Jianghao Wang; Rui Wang
papers.finding: Publisher abstract links new station access with nearby catering establishments and demand.
papers.transfer_limit: Infrastructure opening, not fare change; no coefficient transfer.

papers.title: Exploring the effects of urban rail on the survival of nearby businesses
papers.finding: Publisher abstract reports heterogeneous business-survival effects by type and proximity around rail access.
papers.mvp_use: Do not animate an inevitable immediate business closure.
papers.transfer_limit: Long-run rail investment, not a bus/subway fare change.
